title: stride-engine architecture model
description: Describe your system as trust boundaries, components and data flows. Controls you do not declare are treated as missing.

name.description: Name of the system being modelled.

trustBoundaries.description: Zones of equal trust. Data crossing from one zone to another is where most threats appear.

level.description: How trusted the zone is: 0 is the public internet; higher is more trusted (e.g. 1 edge, 2 private app subnets, 3 isolated data tier).

components.description: Everything that processes, stores or sends data, plus the people and outside systems that use it.

id.description: Unique id, referenced by data flows.

markdownEnumDescriptions: A person who uses the system (customer, employee, administrator).
A web front end or backend-for-frontend that serves pages to browsers.
An API endpoint or gateway that other clients call (e.g. API Gateway, a REST service edge).
A long-running backend service or container (e.g. ECS, EKS pod, EC2 app).
A serverless function (e.g. AWS Lambda).
A database (e.g. RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB).
File or object storage (e.g. S3, a container registry).
An in-memory cache (e.g. ElastiCache Redis).
A message queue or event bus (e.g. SQS, SNS, Kafka).
A sign-in service (e.g. Cognito, Auth0, Okta).
A content delivery network (e.g. CloudFront).
A load balancer or ingress (e.g. ALB, NLB).
Central logging or security monitoring (e.g. CloudTrail + CloudWatch, a SIEM). Add one if you have it.
A third-party system you do not run (payment provider, SaaS, a partner or bank).

trustBoundary.description: Id of the trust boundary this component sits in.

properties.description: Security controls this component has. Anything you leave out is treated as missing.

publicFacing.description: true if it can be reached directly from the internet (public endpoint, public bucket, public IP).

authentication.description: How callers prove who they are: none, basic, api_key, token, oauth or mtls.

authorization.description: true if every request is checked against what this caller may access (per object and per function), not just that they are signed in.

mfa.description: Identity providers only: true if multi-factor authentication is enforced.

inputValidation.description: true if all input is validated against an allow-list schema before use.

logging.description: true if security-relevant actions (or, for data stores, data access) are logged centrally.

rateLimited.description: true if requests are throttled per client.

encryptionAtRest.description: Data stores: true if stored data is encrypted (e.g. KMS-managed keys).

dataClassification.description: The most sensitive data it holds: public, internal, confidential or restricted.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Meant to be public (marketing pages, product images).
Not public, but low harm if leaked (internal ids, configuration).
Harmful if leaked (orders, customer contact details, business data).
Severe harm if leaked: credentials, payment data, health data, government ids.

leastPrivilege.description: true if its IAM role or service account has only the permissions it needs.

privileged.description: true if it runs as root or in a privileged container.

dependencyScanning.description: true if its build scans third-party dependencies (npm audit, Snyk, Dependabot).

redundancy.description: Databases, queues and caches: true if deployed across availability zones or replicated.

waf.description: true if a web application firewall sits in front of it.

dataFlows.description: Data moving from one component to another.

id.description: Unique id for this data flow, e.g. "f1".

from.description: Id of the component that sends the data.

to.description: Id of the component that receives the data.

protocol.description: e.g. https, tls, grpc, grpcs, tcp, sftp, mllp. https, tls, grpcs, mtls, wss and sftp count as encrypted.

encrypted.description: Override whether the channel is encrypted. Leave it out to derive it from the protocol.

authenticated.description: true if the receiver authenticates the sender on this flow. Defaults to false.

dataClassification.description: Most sensitive data on this flow: public, internal, confidential or restricted. Defaults to internal.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Meant to be public (marketing pages, product images).
Not public, but low harm if leaked (internal ids, configuration).
Harmful if leaked (orders, customer contact details, business data).
Severe harm if leaked: credentials, payment data, health data, government ids.

description.description: Optional note shown in tooltips and reports.
